chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who bequeaths a 'share' (sahm) of his wealth, so he said:

"The 'share' is one out of eight, based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Verily, alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to administer the (funds); for those whose hearts have been (to be reconciled) to Truth; for freeing captives or prisoners; for those in debt; for the cause of Allah; and for the wayfarer'..."

key_terms.السَّهْمُ: Share (a specific portion of an estate)
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةٍ: Eight (referring to the eight categories in the verse)
key_terms.لِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ: Based on the saying of Allah (Quranic evidence)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition of 'sahm' (share) in Islamic inheritance and bequests according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the ambiguity of the term 'sahm' in bequests by equating it to one-eighth of the estate, a ruling derived from the eight categories of zakat recipients in Surah At-Tawbah. This interpretation reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking specific legal terms in wills to established Quranic fractions, ensuring that the bequest aligns with the divine distribution of wealth. By citing the verse 'Indeed, zakations are only for the poor...', the Imam establishes a clear jurisprudential precedent for handling vague testamentary gifts.
